workflows.empty: No workflows available. Please create workflows in the admin panel first.
workflows.jobNameHelper: Your name will be appended with each workflow name
workflows.description: Select one or more workflows to run. You can select multiple workflows - each will create its own sequence of job executions. Loopback settings are configured in the workflow itself — a workflow tagged “Loopback” will automatically re-run its eligible steps against newly-cracked passwords.

presetJobs.empty: No preset jobs available. Please create preset jobs in the admin panel first.
presetJobs.jobNameHelper: Your name will be appended with each job type (e.g., 'My Name - Potfile Run')
presetJobs.description: Select one or more preset jobs to run. You can select multiple jobs - they will be created as separate job executions.

loopback.label: Loopback until dry
loopback.helperEligible: Runs the selected job(s), then re-runs the mutatable ones (straight + rules, or a hybrid attack) against only the newly-cracked passwords — repeating until no new cracks are found.
loopback.helperSelectEligible: Select an eligible preset (straight + rules, or a hybrid attack) below to enable loopback.
loopback.helperNoneEligible: None of the selected jobs have a mutation to loop back (they are wordlist-only, brute-force or association).
loopback.helperFilterConflict: Loopback is unavailable while pre-filtering is enabled for this job.
loopback.helperCustom: Runs this attack, then re-runs its mutation (rules or mask) against only the newly-cracked passwords — repeating until no new cracks are found.

filter.enableLabel: Pre-filter the selected wordlist(s) for this job
filter.ephemeralNotice: This filtered list is ephemeral and used only for this job. To create a reusable filtered wordlist, use Wordlist Management. Generation runs in the background; the job starts automatically once it's ready.

association.explainer: Association attack maps each hash to a corresponding wordlist line 1:1. The wordlist line count must match the total hash count ({{hashCount}}).
association.falsePositiveWarning: Note: Association attacks can produce false positives. It is recommended to verify results by downloading cracked hashes, deleting the hashlist, re-uploading, and confirming with a dictionary attack.
association.wordlistHelper: Upload association wordlists via the Hashlist's Association Wordlists section

cloud.allowBurstHelper: Rent GPU instances when the on-prem fleet cannot keep up. Requires the client to be funded and opted in to a provider.
cloud.peerHostsWarning: These are someone else's machines. The host's owner has root over the container, so this client's hashes, wordlists and cracked plaintexts are readable by a third party and are not encrypted at rest on the host. Not recommended for production or client engagement data. Leave this off and the job will still use secure capacity (AWS, RunPod Secure Cloud) if the client allows it.
cloud.maxInstancesHelper: Separate from Max Agents, which governs the on-prem pool. Blank lets the budget decide.

form.jobNameHelper: Leave empty for auto-generated name based on attack configuration
form.incrementModeHelper: Increment tries shorter masks first, growing progressively
form.priorityHelper: Higher priority jobs are executed first (1-1000)
form.chunkDurationHelper: Time in seconds for each chunk (5-86400 seconds)

associationWordlists.mixedWorkFactorsWarning: This hashlist has mixed work factors. Association attacks cannot be run on hashlists with different bcrypt costs or similar variable work factors. You can still upload wordlists, but creating association attack jobs will be blocked.
associationWordlists.explainer: Association wordlists map each hash to a password candidate 1:1 by line number. The wordlist must have exactly {{lines}} lines to match this hashlist's hash count.

clientWordlists.noClientNotice: Client wordlists are only available for hashlists associated with a client.
clientWordlists.description: Client wordlists are available across all hashlists for this client. These can be used with any attack mode, not just association attacks.

allInvalid.body2: Pick the correct type below and click Re-validate — the file stays uploaded, so you don't need to start over.

validationPreview.chooseActionText: Choose Proceed with valid only to import the {{validCount}} valid hashes (listed bad lines will be ignored), or Cancel & fix to delete this upload so you can correct the source file and try again.
